answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token deposit before its votes count, then slash that deposit if later evidence proves coordinated fraud. A newcomer may still join, but multiplying identities no longer multiplies influence for free: the attacker must buy and immobilize capital for every account, risking loss as well as opportunity cost. This makes a sybil plume expensive to sustain across the horizon of a campaign, while a terrace of honest agents can keep participating without staking anew for each interaction.
